newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Central Europe grain exports seen rising.
newsitem.headline: Central Europe grain exports seen rising.

text.p: Increasing grain production will lead to higher exportable surpluses in six central European countries which have applied to join the European Union, an agricultural conference was told on Wednesday.

Grain output in the six applicant countries could climb to 92 million tonnes by 2005 and consumption to 85 million, leaving an exportable surplus of about seven million, Klaus Schumacher of Toepfer International told an Agra Europe conference.
He suggested cereals acreage in the countries would increase one percent per year and yields by 1.8 percent to 3.8 tonnes per hectare by 2005 compared with an EU average of 5.0 tonnes.
"What is more uncertain is the forecast of the increase in consumption of 2.5 percent a year reflecting a forecast growth in population by 0.7 percent and increasing incomes," he said.
Of the total forecast surplus he said approximately five million tonnes would be wheat and the rest corn and barley.

If consumption increased by only two percent a year instead of 2.5 percent the exportable surplus would be about 11 million tonnes but strong domestic consumption growth of three percent a year would leave only some four million tonnes for export.

Although grain exports from the six central European countries will increase the growth is likely to be less dramatic than expected by many analysts but, changes to the Common Agricultural Policy seem necessary to avoid dramatically rising EU grain surpluses, he added.
